SUMMARY:Gelli Printing Collage Workshop
DESCRIPTION:Discover the colorful and creative world of gelli printing in this hands-on collage workshop! Participants will learn how to use a gelli plate to create unique\, layered prints using paint\, textures\, stencils\, and other materials. \nAfter experimenting with different printing techniques\, you’ll use your one-of-a-kind papers to create a finished mixed-media collage. No two pieces will be alike\, and no previous printmaking or art experience is needed. \nThis relaxed and playful workshop is perfect for anyone who enjoys experimenting with color\, pattern\, and texture. \nAll materials are included\, and participants will leave with their own finished collage. \nInstructor: Sarah Soleau

SUMMARY:Fourth Tuesday!
DESCRIPTION:Find. Fathom. Feel. Fourth Tuesdays at the Museum! \nWe are thrilled to introduce Fourth Tuesdays at the Museum! On the fourth Tuesday of every single month\, admission to the galleries is completely FREE for everyone\, proudly sponsored by Bill Lord in honor of Museum founder Edith Barry. \nBut that’s not all. Every Fourth Tuesday brings unique experiences to our spaces: \n\n\nPop-Up History: Get up close with special feature artifacts brought out of the archives just for the day. \n\n\nActivities: Enjoy hands-on activities that connect our local history with contemporary creativity. \n\n\nFresh Perspectives: See something new hidden in plain sight as you tour our current exhibitions. \n\n\nWhether you’re a regular visitor or haven’t stepped through our doors in a while\, this is the perfect excuse to spend an afternoon immersed in community storytelling.
URL:https://www.brickstoremuseum.org/calendar/fourth-tuesday-5/

SUMMARY:Of Seances and Spirits
DESCRIPTION:Step into the mysterious world of turn-of-the-century spiritualism at the Brick Store Museum’s annual Of Séances & Spirits: Supernatural Kennebunk. \nOn Thursday\, October 29\, the Museum’s historic buildings will come alive with stories of mediums\, séances\, ghostly encounters\, and the enduring fascination with the spirit world. Guests will enjoy an evening of immersive experiences inspired by the Spiritualist movement that captivated America in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. \nThroughout the evening\, explore the Museum’s historic campus and discover local stories connected to the supernatural. Learn about Kennebunk’s own connections to séances and spiritualism while enjoying heavy appetizers\, tarot readings\, live performances\, and historical interpretation. \nThe centerpiece of the evening is a timed Victorian-style séance experience featuring first-person historical interpreter Laura Rocklyn as famed medium Mina Crandon\, the “Witch of Lime Street.” Through this engaging and historically informed performance\, guests will encounter the dramatic story of Crandon’s rise to fame and the controversy that surrounded her séances. The experience also explores the lives of two of spiritualism’s most famous figures: Harry Houdini\, who devoted years to exposing fraudulent mediums\, and Sir Arthur Conan Doyle\, creator of Sherlock Holmes and a passionate believer in communication with the dead. \nTickets include access to all activities throughout the evening\, along with a designated séance time. Guests are encouraged to arrive before or remain after their scheduled séance to enjoy the full range of experiences offered across the Museum campus. \nOf Seance and Spirits is generously sponsored by Saco and Biddeford Bank and Tracey Bricker – State Farm Insurance. \nTickets: $60 General Admission | $50 Members \nIncludes one complimentary drink\, heavy appetizers\, a timed séance experience\, live performances\, and access to all Museum activities throughout the evening. \nPlease note: This event takes place throughout the Brick Store Museum’s historic campus and requires walking between buildings. \n  \nIf you are a Museum Member\, your tickets are discounted! Use your Member Code for $10 off each ticket you purchase. You can find your your code in the Member Portal
URL:https://www.brickstoremuseum.org/calendar/of-seances-and-spirits/
LOCATION:Brick Store Museum\, 117 Main Street\, Kennebunk\, ME\, 04043\, United States
ATTACH;FMTTYPE=image/png:https://www.brickstoremuseum.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/seances.png

SUMMARY:Inside History: A Tour Through the Collections
DESCRIPTION:Take an Indoor Walking Tour This Winter! \nIt’s the Museum’s 90th Year! Explore the Brick Store Museum’s own history across five interconnected buildings\, which range from 166 to 216 years old. Once home to businesses\, organizations\, and apartments\, these spaces came together as the Brick Store Museum between 1936 and 1959. \nGo behind the scenes to see highlights from the Museum’s collection of more than 50\,000 artifacts while learning how these historic buildings have evolved over time\, and how the Museum came to be. This guided tour lasts approximately one hour. \nTour ticket includes admission to the Museum exhibitions. \n++ \nAccessibility note: The tour moves through historic buildings and includes uneven flooring and staircases. The Museum’s second floor is not currently wheelchair accessible. \nIf you are a Museum Member\, your tickets are discounted! Use your Member Code for free admission. You can find your your code in the Member Portal

SUMMARY:Fall Foliage Wreath Making Workshop
DESCRIPTION:Celebrate the colors and textures of the season in this hands-on Fall Foliage Wreath Making Workshop! Participants will create a beautiful autumn-inspired wreath using a variety of seasonal materials and foliage. \nWith step-by-step guidance\, you’ll learn how to arrange and layer materials to create a wreath that reflects your own style. Whether you’re new to wreath making or have crafted before\, this relaxed workshop is a wonderful way to get creative and welcome the fall season. \nAll materials are included\, and participants will leave with a finished fall wreath ready to display at home.

SUMMARY:Whimsical Holiday Paper Dolls
DESCRIPTION:Get creative this holiday season by making whimsical paper dolls full of personality! Teaching artist Christine Burgess will guide you step by step as you create Christmas elves\, pets\, or even miniature versions of your family members. \nThese charming creations make wonderful tree decorations\, holiday cards\, or handmade gifts. No art experience is necessary\, and all materials will be provided. Feel free to bring along your favorite painted or scrapbook papers to create unique outfits. \nWarning: This fun and creative process can be addictive! \nInstructor: Christine Burgess\, Teaching Artist

SUMMARY:Jacqueline Schwab | Concerts in West K!
DESCRIPTION:The Museum’s Concert Partner Mousam River Music Presents: \nJacqueline Schwab\, returning for a special performance at the First Parish Church at 114 Main Street\, across the street from the Museum. From the soundtracks of Ken Burns’ documentaries to the White House to the PBS American Roots special with The American Pops Orchestra\, pianist Jacqueline Schwab is known for evoking the American musical past\, but in a fresh\, personal way. \n+++ \nPre-purchase tickets are available through this site until Saturday\, December 5 at noon. Afterward\, walk-ins are welcome unless otherwise noted! \n+++ \nNote: Museum Member Discounts are not available for the Mousam River Music Concert Series as all income is split with performers.

SUMMARY:Metal Embossed Ornament Workshop
DESCRIPTION:Create a beautiful\, one-of-a-kind ornament using the art of metal embossing! In this hands-on workshop\, participants will use lightweight tin or copper foil and simple drawing tools to press and emboss their own designs into the metal. \nChoose from provided patterns or create a design of your own\, then add texture and details to make your ornament unique. SUMMARY:Inside History: A Tour Through the Collections
DESCRIPTION:Take an Indoor Walking Tour This Winter! \nIt’s the Museum’s 90th Year! Explore the Brick Store Museum’s own history across five interconnected buildings\, which range from 166 to 216 years old. Once home to businesses\, organizations\, and apartments\, these spaces came together as the Brick Store Museum between 1936 and 1959. \nGo behind the scenes to see highlights from the Museum’s collection of more than 50\,000 artifacts while learning how these historic buildings have evolved over time\, and how the Museum came to be. SUMMARY:Sparkling at 90: A Historic Holiday Soiree at the Nathanial Lord Thompson House
DESCRIPTION:Step into the magic of the season at one of Kennebunk’s most treasured historic homes\, the Nathaniel Lord Thompson House\, known as the home of Kennebunk’s very first Christmas tree! \nJoin the Brick Store Museum on Sunday\, December 13\, 2026\, from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM\, for a festive afternoon celebrating the warmth\, elegance\, and traditions of Christmases past. \nExplore this beautiful historic home\, decorated for the holidays\, while enjoying seasonal appetizers\, sweet treats\, and holiday cheer. Discover the fascinating history of the house and the Christmas traditions that have made it such a special part of Kennebunk’s story. \nThis special event offers a rare opportunity to experience the charm of a 19th-century Kennebunk Christmas\, surrounded by festive decorations\, historic architecture\, and good company. \nTickets: $90 per person \nMuseum Members save $10 per ticket! Use your Member Code at checkout to receive your discount. You can find your code in the Member Portal. \nAdvance reservations are strongly encouraged\, as space is limited. \nMember discounts are available exclusively to current Brick Store Museum Members. Registrations will be checked against our membership list. \nWe look forward to celebrating the holiday season with you!
